name: Wall Slide
summary: A scapular mobility and activation exercise sliding the forearms vertically against a wall to engage the serratus anterior and promote upward rotation.

setup: Stand facing a flat wall in a staggered or hip-width stance, roughly one foot away.
Place your forearms flat against the wall, parallel to each other, with elbows bent at 90 degrees and at shoulder height.
Gently protract your shoulder blades so your upper back feels broad, without rounding the thoracic spine.
steps: Maintain light, consistent pressure against the wall through your forearms and wrists.
Slide your forearms upward along the wall in a slow, controlled motion, allowing your shoulder blades to upwardly rotate.
Continue sliding upward until your arms reach overhead without arching your lower back or shrugging your shoulders into your ears.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly slide your forearms back down to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you prepare, exhale smoothly while sliding upward, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
cues: Push the wall away with your forearms
Keep ribs down and core braced

common_faults.fault: Excessively arching the lower back to gain overhead reach.
common_faults.correction: Engage the abdominals to keep the ribs anchored down and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Elbows flaring outward or lifting off the wall during the upward slide.
common_faults.correction: Maintain gentle inward tension so forearms stay parallel and in continuous contact with the wall.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the upper traps excessively rather than rotating the scapulae upward.
common_faults.correction: Focus on driving the movement by pushing the bottom tips of the shoulder blades around the ribcage.

precautions: Limit overhead range of motion if you experience shoulder impingement or pain.
